Live Captions-specific listing vocabulary — what translates differently

Real-time caption marketing on App Store pages uses vocabulary general utility guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese buyers describe Live Captions workflows — not a literal paste of US marketing:

Live Captions vs Closed Captions vs generic subtitles

US pages use "Live Captions", "Live Caption", "Real-time captions", or "Conversation captions." China storefront copy often uses 实时字幕 for Apple's Accessibility feature name, 实时字幕显示 for the display benefit, or 对话字幕 for conversation-specific captions — depending on whether you mean system Live Captions, in-app meeting subtitles, or FaceTime caption overlays. AppLocale aligns phrasing with your actual caption scope and avoids conflating Live Captions with 隐藏式字幕 (Closed Captions + SDH embedded tracks) when your screenshots show real-time speech-to-text, not baked-in media subtitle files.

Conversation captions vs media captions vs call captions

Screenshot galleries may label FaceTime subtitle bars (对话字幕), phone call captions (通话字幕), and media playback subtitles (媒体实时字幕) separately. Buyers searching for deaf and hard-of-hearing tools distinguish conversation accessibility from meeting transcription — match the caption workflows your English listing and screenshots actually show.

Live Captions vs Sound Recognition vs Live Speech

Three speech-adjacent Accessibility features share English marketing vocabulary indie teams conflate. 实时字幕 (Live Captions) displays heard speech as text. 声音识别 (Sound Recognition) alerts for ambient sounds like baby crying. 实时语音 / 键入朗读 (Live Speech) speaks typed text aloud. Each term signals different buyer intent — do not reuse Sound Recognition or Live Speech keywords on Live Captions screenshots.

AppLocale FAQ

Does AppLocale implement Speech framework or real-time caption players?

No. We deliver Connect listing metadata copy only — name, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text when included, and screenshot caption lines. Speech framework integration, SFSpeechRecognizer pipelines, and caption overlay UI engineering are outside scope.

How is Live Captions listing copy different from Sound Recognition, Live Speech, or Dictation?

Live Captions listing copy covers real-time speech-to-text subtitles for conversations, FaceTime, phone calls, and media — displaying heard speech as readable text on screen. Sound Recognition covers ambient sound alerts like baby crying and smoke alarms. Live Speech covers type-to-speak — users type text and hear it spoken aloud. Dictation covers voice typing into text fields. Those are separate scopes with different screenshot vocabulary.

How is this different from Voice Control, Speak Screen, or Closed Captions?

Voice Control covers hands-free UI operation with spoken commands on the local device. Speak Screen and Spoken Content cover reading on-screen content aloud to the user. Closed Captions + SDH covers embedded subtitle tracks on media files. Live Captions covers real-time speech-to-text subtitle overlays for live conversations and playback — a different buyer story on each surface.

Should my zh-Hans listing claim to replace iOS Live Captions in Settings?

Only if your app actually provides that capability and your English listing already states it accurately. AppLocale rewrites from your source claims — we do not invent system-replacement promises or certify parity with Apple's Accessibility Live Captions feature.
